long_biography.plain_text:
For food distributor John Pappas, the location of a warehouse mattered as much as its size. Bringing specialist businesses close together allowed orders for different ingredients to travel on one truck. In New England, this helped the group accept small orders without requiring customers to meet separate minimums at each supplier.

He also introduced more structured methods into acquired businesses. Warehouse staff moved from voice-directed picking to scanning systems that guided them to products and signalled incorrect selections. Shared operating measures, including delivery mileage, truck capacity and cost per case, gave managers a consistent way to compare sites and plan routes.
